newsitem.title: USA: Scattered showers seen moving across U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Scattered showers seen moving across U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Scattered showers should move through the U.S. Midwest late this week and next week, providing moderate moisture for crops, meteorologists said.
Temperatures may temporarily climb to 90 degrees Fahrenheit this weekend, but meteorologists said passing cold fronts should prevent a week-long heat wave.
"It looks like the pattern for the Midwest is just about ideal (for crops) the next 10 days," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Burgio said there was no indication in weather maps of a high pressure ridge developing over the Midwest.

Showers and cooler weather will spread across much of the Midwest beginning late Wednesday. Warmer weather should return Friday in the western Midwest, with highs from the mid 80s to low 90s, and spread to the east Saturday, he said.
More showers were due in the western areas Saturday and Sunday and again Tuesday through Wednesday of next week, he said.
Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, said recent rains have replenished soil moisture in nearly all of the Midwest areas.
The only remaining dry location was in central Illinois bordered by Peoria, Champagne and Springfield.
"Another five or six days of dryness and they will have a problem," he said of farmers in that area.
In the next few days this area could receive 0.10 to 0.50 inch, Gesser said, which would not be enough to replenish soil moisture.
Elsewhere in the Midwest, Gesser said scattered showers and thunderstorms should occur through July 4.
